expectations.text: Models at least one negative-spillover scenario per shortlisted candidate and what it would cost Solane
expectations.evidence: Only 2 of the 11 candidates get any spillover modeling. Halvern is the strongest case: the 'Junior-partner effect' is named explicitly ('Halvern's audience sees Solane as a discount extension, and *your* 95€-basket positioning gets diluted rather than elevated') — a real downside scenario with a stated cost to Solane's positioning. Marisse Bell gets a thinner one: a fraud/inflated-follower risk with a hand-waved cost ('a fraud scandal costs more than the fee'), which is an assertion rather than a modeled consequence. The remaining 9 candidates receive no spillover analysis at all — the answer
